PUBLIC RESPONSE: There is no credible record of Goodluck Ebele Jonathan ever publicly “identifying himself as Azikiwe” in the sense of renouncing Jonathan as a family name and adopting Azikiwe as a personal/family identification.

Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan is the full name under which he has been known in official Nigerian records. Azikiwe is a middle name, not a surname he has ever used to identify himself. The element was long present in his birth and civil records and it is the name under which he was sworn in as Acting President 9 February 2010 and as substantive President 29 May 2010.

The name only became a matter of public controversy because it was very widely reproduced when the Independent National Electoral Commission published his nomination papers for the 2015 presidential election in December 2014. That is the first time the full string Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan was mass-circulated in the press and therefore the first time the Azikiwe middle name was noticed by a broad public audience. No separate act of public self-identification as “Azikiwe” in place of Jonathan ever took place.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: There is no credible public record of Goodluck Ebele Jonathan ever adopting or publicly identifying himself as “Azikiwe”.

His legal and consistently used public name is Goodluck Ebele Jonathan, GCFR, born 20 November 1957. The suffix “Azikiwe” is not part of his birth name and he has never claimed it in a speech, oath, autobiography or official declaration.

What does exist is a persistent mis-attribution / clerical error. The name “Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan” first appeared in the public domain on the INEC nomination / affidavit papers that were filed for the 2015 general election, circulated in late 2014 / early 2015. The appearance was widely reported as an error and was never adopted or affirmed by Jonathan himself. In other words the “Azikiwe” string is an erroneous addition to his name in secondary sources, not a self-identification by the former President. There is therefore no year in which he publicly identified himself as Azikiwe.

There is no verifiable year of public self-identification as “Azikiwe”.

Goodluck Ebele Jonathan is the name consistently used in his public acts, speeches, state papers and as recorded in the oath of office transcripts. There is no speech, oath reading, signature, autobiographical statement or credible press report in which he introduces himself, signs or is documented as identifying himself simply as “Azikiwe” or as having replaced Jonathan with Azikiwe.

Azikiwe is at most a middle name in the formal string Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan, not a public alias/surname he uses to identify himself. In common and official usage he is Goodluck Ebele Jonathan / Goodluck Jonathan.

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: No verifiable year exists. There is no credible record of Goodluck Ebele Jonathan ever publicly self-identifying as “Azikiwe” or adopting Azikiwe as a stand-alone alias / replacement for Jonathan.

The name that is consistently used in all of his official public acts, oaths of office, INEC nomination forms, state papers and his own speeches is Goodluck Ebele Jonathan, in common usage Goodluck Jonathan. 

The string “Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan” is a biographical accretion. It was first mass-circulated to the Nigerian public when INEC published the nomination/affidavit papers for the 2015 general election in late 2014/early 2015. That publication generated the widespread 2014/2015 controversy and was widely reported in the Nigerian press as a clerical error that was never adopted or affirmed by Jonathan himself. He has never introduced himself, signed a public document or spoken as “Azikiwe” or as Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan.

The claim that Azikiwe is a long-standing middle name first visible in the 2007 nomination cycle / 2010 oath, and the claim that he publicly identified himself as Azikiwe in 2007, are both unsupported by contemporaneous public statements, oath transcripts and press reporting. The record shows a consistently used public name Goodluck Ebele Jonathan and no documented moment of public self-identification as Azikiwe. Hence there is no year to report.

PUBLIC RESPONSE:

I am aligning with Colleagues 1, 2, 3 and 5 on the core evidentiary point and I do not find Colleague 4’s 2007 claim supported.

I therefore see no credible year for a genuine public self-identification as Azikiwe.
